Subject: Sudden throughput drop on our Dedicated pool — urgent

Diego,

We started seeing a sharp increase in request queueing and 500-level errors against our dedicated GPU pool this morning around 08:05 PDT. Latency jumped from ~120ms to multiple seconds and a small percentage of requests returned 503/500. Our app is fairly sensitive to tail latency — we saw a 30% degradation in successful inference throughput, and several clients reported timeouts.

We’re on Dedicated (pool-id: acm-plate-7) with a reserved commit. Can you confirm whether this is on your side, and what the next steps are? I’ve attached a short slice of our client-side logs showing the timestamps and error types.

High level: we need (1) acknowledgement and ETA for remediation, (2) whether there will be billing credit for degraded service, and (3) a timeline for a formal incident report.

Thanks,
Daniel

Subject: INTERNAL: Acme Robotics P1 — Dedicated pool degradation (pool acm-plate-7)

Team — forwarding Daniel's note below. Immediate asks:
1) Monica/hannah: check GPU pool health, autoscaler decisions, and any recent control-plane changes. Share the earliest packet/heartbeat gaps you see.
2) If the autoscaler marked nodes Unhealthy and paused scaling, can we manually force a restart of the pool and bring nodes back into service as a mitigation?
3) Marissa: please open a HubSpot incident record and keep the customer communication cadence at 30/60/120 minutes.

Initial context from telemetry (very preliminary):
- Marketplace scheduler reported missed heartbeats for a subset of nodes in acm-plate-7 between 07:58–08:07 PDT.
- The controller interpreted that as node failures and moved nodes to maintenance, which reduced available capacity; autoscaler inhibited scale-ups while nodes were being reaped.

Mitigation proposal (short term):
- Roll back the heartbeat-stricter check deployed in the last maintenance window (2:00 AM PDT).
- Restart pod group for acm-plate-7 to rejoin nodes.
- Temporarily relax autoscaler inhibition to allow immediate scale-up while we validate health.

Please reply with status updates and any logs attached. I’m coordinating external comms.

Thanks,
Diego

Date: 2026-10-05T22:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident update: ACME Dedicated pool (acm-plate-7) — root cause and next steps

Daniel / Lisa — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Below is the concise post-incident summary and planned remediation steps. I’ve attached a draft RCA PDF with timelines and logs for your records (redwood_rca_draft.pdf).

What happened (summary):
- Between 07:58–08:10 PDT on 2026-10-03, the Dedicated pool acm-plate-7 experienced intermittent heartbeat loss between the pool agent and the controller. A recently deployed heartbeat validation change (rolled out 02:00 PDT) made the controller more aggressive in marking nodes Unhealthy after a short heartbeat gap.
- The controller marked ~18% of nodes as Unhealthy in two waves, which temporarily reduced available capacity. The autoscaler’s protection logic paused scale-ups while node reaping was underway, which prevented immediate replenishment of capacity. The combined effect led to queued requests and elevated 5xx rates for customer traffic.

Immediate mitigation we applied (Oct 3):
- Rolled back the strict heartbeat validation in the controller and restarted the pool agent group for acm-plate-7 — capacity returned to normal within ~22 minutes.
- We adjusted the autoscaler inhibition window to avoid pausing scale-ups for transient heartbeat losses.
- Engineering patched the monitoring alert to differentiate transient network blips vs. sustained heartbeat loss.

Root cause:
- A conservative heartbeat change increased sensitivity to transient network jitter; autoscaler protection logic combined with the reaping sequence created a temporary capacity hole.

Customer impact:
- Window: 2026-10-03 07:58–08:20 PDT.
- Users impacted: Acme Robotics production traffic on acm-plate-7.
- Symptoms: increased queueing, higher tail latency, ~30% reduction in successful throughput for affected requests, short-lived 5xx spike.

What we’re doing to prevent recurrence (timeline):
- Short-term (now): autoscaler inhibition logic refined, improved alerting thresholds, and a follow-up validation run across all Dedicated pools (complete).
- Medium-term (next 2 weeks): formal canary and staged rollout guard for heartbeat/controller changes; expanded integration tests for controller–agent heartbeats.
- Long-term (next 60 days): autoscaler rewrite to decouple reaping from immediate scale decisions and deeper post-deployment smoke tests for control-plane changes.

Customer remediation:
- We will apply a one-time service credit for the impacted interval; Marissa (copied) will follow up with the concrete credit amount and process.
- If you prefer a technical postmortem call, we can schedule a 30-minute session early next week with engineering and SRE.

Attachments: redwood_rca_draft.pdf (RCA draft with logs), ops_log_excerpt.txt (SRE-extracted controller logs snippet), gpu_pool_dashboard_screenshot.png (utilization around incident window).

Next steps for you:
- Marissa will reach out with the credit details and to propose a time for the postmortem call.
- Please share any additional request IDs or client traces you want correlated to the attached logs; we’ll add them to the final RCA.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know Dedicated capacity is core to your production SLAs and we’re treating this seriously.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
